summary: Jadunath Sarkar was an Indian historian and archaeologist who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta (M.A. ~1892). He held posts at Patna College (1899–1926) and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Jae-gwon Kim earned a PhD from Ryukoku University in 2007 and subsequently held a post there.
Jagaddhar Zadoo was an Indologist who worked at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, where his posts are attested between 1924 and 1930 and as Superintendent in 1947.

Jagadish Chandra Chatterji was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge. In 1911, he is attested as Director of the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Jagannath Upadhyaya was a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1980–1983) and became the first director of the Rare Buddhist Text Research Project at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies in 1985.

Jagdish Kashyap, an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Patna College, Banaras Hindu University, and under Rahul Sankrityayan. He taught Pāli at BHU and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Srikrishna Harihirlekar, Nankoo Bhaya Telang, and Swami Lakshman Joo. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chaired the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

Jake H. Davis is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Marlboro College, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the CUNY Graduate Center. He has taught at Brown University (attested 2013–2018) and held appointments at NYU and BCBS.

Jakob Steiner studied at Heidelberg University (1818–1821) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at the Basel Mission, Oxford, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He served as professor at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and held a chair at Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and held faculty positions at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University.

James A. Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held posts at California State University (attested 1998) and served as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).
James Adam was a scholar of philosophy who completed his studies at the University of Aberdeen (~1876–1880) and Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884).

James Alan Matisoff is a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who studied at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley. He taught at Columbia University (1966–1969) before serving as a professor at UC Berkeley (1970–2002).

James Atkinson, a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, was educated at the University of Edinburgh. He served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818 and held posts at the India Government Mint, Kolkata.

James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his graduate education and received his PhD in 1996 from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he studied under doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne.

James Blumenthal was a Buddhist studies scholar and tibetologist who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He taught at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

James Burgess was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the universities of Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India from 1873, holding the post of Director General from 1886 to 1889.

James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundup Sopa. Around 1975, he became an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa.

James C. Dobbins is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Yale University in 1984 and later served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).
